title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors; key management personnel and direct reports to the CEO; corporate and divisional accounting officers reporting directly to KMP; secretaries and assistants performing confidential work and reporting to Directors or KMP; employees with access to the Group's financial results before release; and other persons who regularly possess inside information and have been told by the Company Secretary that they are a Restricted Person. All the substantive restrictions (blackouts, prior written approval for every trade, the speculative and short-term ban, the unvested hedging ban and post-trade notification) apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company. A sub-set of Restricted Persons, distinguished only for the approval route: the Chairman approves Directors' trades and another Director approves the Chairman's.

tiers.name: key management personnel
tiers.description: Key management personnel of the Company, notified as such by the Company Secretary. Subject to all Restricted Person obligations plus the additional requirement to obtain approval for any margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities, which may be granted on conditions.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Person in dealings with Company securities (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependants), and any company or other entity the Restricted Person is able to control. Restricted Persons must take reasonable steps to ensure Connected Persons only trade where the Restricted Person could, including by obtaining clearance for the Connected Person's trading.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement to the ASX of the full-year results
the day following the announcement to the ASX of the half-year results
the day following the release to the ASX of the March Quarterly Report
the day following the release to the ASX of the September Quarterly Report

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time (s15(e)). Separately, the Company may notify Restricted Persons that they must not trade, either for a specified period or until further notice (s5(b)). The Policy does not say whether such notices are confidential, but a refusal or revocation of approval must be kept confidential (s22).

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named. A purchased put and written call over vested Company securities is an arrangement that operates to limit economic risk and so is a hedging arrangement, which is permitted provided it complies with the rest of the Policy: prior written approval, execution within 7 days, outside blackout periods, and post-trade notification. No venue restriction, so an OTC structure with a bank is covered.
rules.evidence: Any other hedging arrangements involving Company securities must comply with the requirements of this Policy.

rules.detail: Any derivative over unvested Company securities, including equity incentives under the Equity Incentive Plan, that limits economic risk is prohibited outright; there is no approval route.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements over any unvested Company securities (including equity incentives issued under the Company's Equity Incentive Plan) to which they may be entitled.

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition on hedging unvested securities, extending to securities 'to which they may be entitled', so unvested rights and performance awards are covered as well as issued but unvested shares.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements over any unvested Company securities (including equity incentives issued under the Company's Equity Incentive Plan) to which they may be entitled.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested securities is expressly permitted but must comply with the Policy: prior written approval from the Chairman (Directors) or CEO or delegate (other Restricted Persons), which may be refused without reasons or granted on conditions, execution within 7 days, no blackout period, satisfaction of the front page test, and prompt notification to the Company Secretary afterwards.
rules.evidence: Any other hedging arrangements involving Company securities must comply with the requirements of this Policy.

rules.detail: The ban bites only on unvested securities. Once plan securities have vested but remain held under the plan, hedging is not prohibited, but any trading in those securities once they cease to be held under the plan must be in accordance with the Policy, so approval and the blackout rules apply.
rules.evidence: where securities in the Company granted under an equity incentive plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any trading in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar with funding or similar structure operates to limit the economic risk of holding Company securities and is therefore a hedging arrangement caught by section 28: prohibited over unvested securities, otherwise permitted subject to approval, blackouts and notification. The substance over form approach in section 2 means the label given to the structure will not determine the analysis.
rules.evidence: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned. A short sale would in practice be caught by the ban on speculative or short-term trading in section 25 and by the front page test, but the Policy contains no express short selling prohibition.

Securities lending is not mentioned and there is no definition of trading that would obviously catch a lend and return with no change in beneficial interest; section 34(c) would arguably exclude it as trading with no effective change to the beneficial interest.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities operates to limit or alter economic risk and would be treated as a hedging arrangement requiring compliance with the Policy; in practice a CFD position would also usually offend the ban on speculative or short-term trading in section 25.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade the Company's securities on a speculative or short-term trading basis.

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted, not prohibited. KMP must obtain approval through the ordinary sections 20 to 24 process, and the Company may impose any conditions it sees fit, expressly including conditions on the circumstances in which Company securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: Key management personnel must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in sections 20-24 for any margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending approval requirement sits under the heading 'Additional restrictions applying to key management personnel' and is expressed to apply only to KMP. For a Restricted Person who is not KMP the Policy is silent on margin lending, though any resulting trade in securities would still need approval.
rules.evidence: ADDITIONAL RESTRICTIONS APPLYING TO KEY MANAGEMENT PERSONNEL - MARGIN LENDING ARRANGEMENTS

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, charge, pledge or other security interest over Company securities is not mentioned and is not brought within the description of trading in section 7, which covers buying, selling, agreeing to buy or sell, exercising options, and applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities. The only recognition of an encumbrance is indirect, through the margin lending approval for KMP and the excluded trading carve-out for a secured lender's enforcement sale.

The only secured financing expressly regulated is a 'margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities', which requires approval and may be made conditional. A bank loan secured on collared shares is not named; given the substance over form approach in section 2 it should be treated as within section 32 and approval sought. The Policy positively contemplates secured lending by excluding a secured lender's enforcement sale from the blackout, approval and short-term rules.
rules.evidence: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 32 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).

rules.detail: No defined period; a general prohibition on speculative or short-term trading. Selling shares received on vesting of equity incentive entitlements is expressly not a short-term trade, and section 34 disapplies the prohibition to plan participation, DRP, SPP and rights issue acquisitions, takeover or buy-back disposals, no-change-of-beneficial-interest trades, pre-approved non-discretionary trading plans and secured lender enforcement sales.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade the Company's securities on a speculative or short-term trading basis.

clearance.approver: the Chairman or their delegate; for the Chairman's own trades, another Director
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: Following receipt of approval to trade, the approved trade must occur within 7 days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: A request for approval to trade will be answered as soon as practicable. The approver may: a) grant or refuse the request. b) impose conditions on the trade.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: During any period that is not a blackout period under section 15, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed trade, obtain written approval for the proposed trade of the Company's securities.

participation in an equity incentive plan operated by the Company
acquisition through a dividend reinvestment plan, a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders, or a rights issue
disposal through acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

short_term.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade the Company's securities on a speculative or short-term trading basis. Selling shares received following the vesting of entitlements under an equity incentive plan is not a short-term trade.

exceptions.approver: Chairman, another Director, or the CEO or their delegate under section 20
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

exceptions.approver: Chairman, another Director, or the CEO or their delegate under section 20
exceptions.evidence: If a Restricted Person needs to trade securities during a blackout period due to exceptional circumstances and is not in possession of any Inside Information, then, they may apply for approval to trade.
a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

participation in an equity incentive plan operated by the Company. However, where securities in the Company granted under an equity incentive plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any trading in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy.
acquisition of Company securities through a dividend reinvestment plan.
the disposal of Company securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back.

trading that results in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary).

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price or LVR trigger is prescribed, but the Company may condition its approval of a margin lending arrangement, expressly including 'with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call' (s33).
financing_disclosure: key management personnel; before entering into any margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities; approval request to the CEO or their delegate (Chairman for Directors); prior to the arrangement (s32)
Restricted Persons; following any trade; to the Company Secretary; promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into (s29)

exemption_authority: Sections 16 to 18: a Restricted Person who needs to trade during a blackout period because of exceptional circumstances (likely severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order) and who holds no Inside Information may apply for approval, which is granted only on sufficient evidence, in the approver's opinion, that the trade is a reasonable course of action. The approvers are those in section 20, and approval will not be granted where the trade would fail the front page test (s11).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 15, 19 and 25 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares is expressly outside the blackout, prior approval and short-term trading rules, so lender remedies survive even in a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 32 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can dictate LVR or sale-trigger terms as a condition of approving the loan, so the facility terms must be agreed with the Company before the bank commits.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar cannot be structured around the unvested hedging ban or the margin lending approval by relabelling the instrument or using a Connected Person.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for trading under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the trade would not satisfy the test set out in section 9 above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval of the collar can be refused purely on perception grounds, independently of inside information or blackouts, and the approver need not give reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: During any period that is not a blackout period under section 15, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed trade, obtain written approval for the proposed trade of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no free trading window at all: entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement of the collar each need fresh written approval, valid for only 7 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval can be withdrawn after the term sheet is agreed but before execution, creating settlement risk for the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade Company securities during ... the period from 4.00pm (Sydney time) on 31 March each year until the day following the release to the ASX of the March Quarterly Report.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly as well as half and full year blackouts leave short and irregular open periods, so collar entry and any scheduled roll must be timed around four blackouts plus any Board-imposed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take reasonable steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only trade securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to trade under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar booked through a spouse, family trust or controlled company must itself be cleared, so the counterparty entity does not avoid the approval requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements over any unvested Company securities (including equity incentives issued under the Company's Equity Incentive Plan) to which they may be entitled.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Sizing must be limited to vested holdings, and the wording 'to which they may be entitled' extends the ban to unvested rights and future entitlements, not just issued shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Company has notified the Restricted Persons that they must not trade securities (either for a specified period, or until the Company gives further notice).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-ended trading ban can be imposed at any time and may block delivery or unwind indefinitely, so the collar documentation needs a settlement deferral mechanism.

summary: A funded collar is possible for a Whitehaven Director or KMP over vested shares, and this policy is unusually accommodating of the financing leg. The put and call are not named but are hedging arrangements under section 27, which section 28 permits over vested securities provided the Policy is complied with; the loan is regulated only as a 'margin lending arrangement' requiring KMP approval under section 32, and the Company may impose conditions including on when shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call. Critically, section 34(e) excludes a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights from the blackout, prior approval and short-term trading rules, so enforcement is not itself a breach. The practical constraints are that every trade, including collar entry, roll and unwind, needs prior written approval that is valid for only 7 days, may be conditioned or revoked at any time and may be refused on front page test grounds, and must fall outside four annual blackouts plus any Board-imposed period; each trade must then be notified to the Company Secretary the same day. Unvested securities, including entitlements the executive may become entitled to, cannot be hedged at all.
